BETWEEN:-
 VISHAL S/O PRAKASH CHANDRA LAHOTI, AGED 25  YEAR S, 11, MAHANKAL MARG, BAGLI, DIST-DEWAS  (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI RITESH INANI - ADVOCATE)

AND  THE STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH THROUGH  P.S.BAGLI DISTRICT DEWAS (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 ( SHRI KAPIL MAHANT - PANEL LAWYER)
 (MS. APOORVA SHUKLA - ADVOCATE FOR OBJECTOR)
 This application coming on for admission this day, the   following:
 ORDER

This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No. 416/2023 registered at Police Station Bagli District Dewas (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 506 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
2.

As per prosecution story, prosecutrix on 11.8.2023 lodged an FIR at police station Bagli District Dewas by stating that in the year 2019 she was preparing computer coaching in a private institute,
the present applicant was also came there for preparation.
They exchanged mobile numbers and used to talk on mobile.

In August 2019, applicant came to house of prosecutrix and told her that she loves her and wanted to marry with her and on that basis, applicant established physical relationship with her and thereafter repeated same act.
In January 2023 when prosecutrix asked her for marriage, the applicant denied to marry with her and forced her that if she tells anything about the incident then he will kill her.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 27.9.2023.
Prosecutrix is a 25 years old matured and major lady.
FIR is about 3 years delayed.
No offence under section 376 and 506 IPC is made out against the applicant.
The physical relationships were established with consent of the prosecutrix.
He is permanent resident of Dewas District.
Investigation is over and charge sheet has been filed.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by stating that prosecutrix has supported case of prosecution in her statement under section 164 Cr.P.C.
5.

Counsel for objector opposes the prayer and prays for its rejection by stating that family members of applicant are still threatening and pressurizing her for compromise, therefore he does not deserve for bail.

6. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.
7.

After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix is a 25 years old matured lady, she remained in the company of applicant for a period of three and half years, FIR is so much delayed, but final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE BDJ Vishal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199433868/
